strengths: 3rd-largest district economy in Karnataka — GDDP Rs 99,067 crore (2023-24), 3.9% of state GSDP
Aequs Aerospace SEZ — India's first aerospace precision-manufacturing SEZ (since 2009, 250+ acres), supplying Airbus, Boeing, Safran, Collins; group revenue ~Rs 1,000 cr, IPO Dec 2025
Among India's largest foundry & hydraulic-cylinder clusters — ~160 MSME foundries, ~7,500 jobs (Udyambag belt)
Karnataka's #1 sugarcane district ('Sugar Bowl of Karnataka') — 24 sugar factories, ~1/3 of the state's mills, large ethanol & co-generation base
Healthy and improving bank credit — CD ratio 77.4% (Mar 2025, up from 69.8% in 2023), above the state norm
Strong surface-water endowment — Hidkal (Ghataprabha, 51 TMC) and Navilatirtha (Malaprabha, 38 TMC) reservoirs; Krishna, Ghataprabha & Malaprabha rivers

challenges: Per-capita income only Rs 1.63 lakh (2023-24) — about half the state average despite the large aggregate economy
Severe groundwater stress in the eastern blocks — 4 Over-Exploited and 1 Critical (Athani, Saundatti, Ramdurg, Bailahongal, Kagavada)
Irrigation is groundwater-dominant (~71% from wells/borewells, only ~17% canal) — exposed where aquifers are over-drawn
Sharp east–west divide: dry, over-pumped east vs assured-rainfall western belt
Health-facility shortfall against population norms, especially Community Health Centres (8 vs ~40 norm)
Foundry cluster needs modernization — energy efficiency, cleaner melt, effluent compliance (core data dates to 2015-16)
Sugar economy is water-intensive and exposed to cane-price / arrear cycles
IT base is early — a dedicated IT park is still proposed (blocked on Ministry of Defence land), tech firms ~70 with ~Rs 150 cr turnover
opportunities: Raise per-capita income toward the state average by lifting productivity across the existing industrial base
Deepen the Aequs-anchored aerospace ecosystem with tier-2/3 precision suppliers and MRO (Magellan JV, 2025)
Modernize the foundry cluster toward cleaner processes and EV / new-energy components
Scale sugar-linked ethanol and co-generation — Ugar (845 KLPD) and Renuka (500 KLPD) already expanded under the biofuel push
Convert the over-exploited eastern belt to drip, recharge and canal/lift irrigation off the Krishna–Ghataprabha–Malaprabha system
Build the Hubballi-Dharwad-Belagavi tech cluster and land the proposed ~750-acre IT/semiconductor park
Expand food processing and dairy value chains; heritage & nature tourism (Kittur, Saundatti Yellamma, Gokak Falls)

summary.note: Belagavi's eastern blocks are severely stressed — 4 Over-Exploited and 1 Critical. Irrigation is ~71% groundwater-based, so this is the binding constraint. Khanapur (11.7%) and Kitthuru (42.1%) in the west retain real headroom.

groundwater.roadmapImplication: Halt new groundwater extraction in Athani, Saundatti, Ramdurg, Bailahongal and Kagavada — shift to drip, artificial recharge and canal/surface-lift off the Ghataprabha and Malaprabha commands. New groundwater-based irrigation only has headroom in Khanapur and Kitthuru.

dc.headline: Belagavi is Karnataka's 3rd-largest district economy (GDDP Rs 99,067 cr) yet per-capita income is only Rs 1.63L — about half the state average. The agenda is raising productivity across a strong but under-leveraged base, while fixing the eastern-belt groundwater crisis.

water.headline: Five eastern blocks are Over-Exploited or Critical and ~71% of district irrigation is groundwater-based. The programme must cut extraction and shift to the Ghataprabha (Hidkal, 51 TMC) and Malaprabha (Navilatirtha, 38 TMC) surface commands — only Khanapur and Kitthuru retain headroom.

actions.title: Extend Ghataprabha / Malaprabha canal & lift command

agriculture.headline: Karnataka's #1 sugarcane district (137,630 ha cane) plus maize, soybean and Nippani bidi tobacco — running into a groundwater wall in the east. The shift is extraction-led to efficiency-led: drip, cane diversification and value addition.

actions.title: Drip conversion in cane-growing stressed blocks

industrial.headline: Belagavi has an industrial base most districts lack: the Aequs aerospace SEZ (IPO-listed, supplying Airbus/Boeing), ~160 foundries (~7,500 jobs), and 24 sugar mills. The agenda is deepening and modernization — and converting that base into higher per-capita income.

actions.title: Aerospace tier-2/3 supplier park (Aequs ecosystem + MRO)

health.headline: 660 public facilities serve 47.8 lakh people, but Community Health Centres (8 vs ~40 norm) and sub-centres are well short. Secondary care is the binding gap.

actions.title: New CHCs against the norm shortfall
Sub-centre / PHC strengthening in under-served taluks

education.headline: Literacy at 73.5%. The opportunity is aligning skilling to the district's own clusters — aerospace (Aequs), foundry, sugar-tech and the HDB IT cluster.

kdem.headline: Belagavi sits in the Hubballi-Dharwad-Belagavi (HDB) Beyond Bengaluru cluster, with ~70 tech firms and rare deep-tech anchors (aerospace SEZ, foundry) to build Industry 4.0 around. The dedicated ~750-acre IT/semiconductor park is the key unlock — currently stalled on land.

actions.title: Land the ~750-acre IT / semiconductor park (MoD land)

minister.headline: Belagavi: 47.8 lakh people, Karnataka's 3rd-largest district economy (GDDP Rs 99,067 cr) — but per-capita income only Rs 1.63L and a serious eastern-belt groundwater crisis. Indicative Rs 18,500 Cr scaffold across 3 phases to raise productivity and incomes.

digitalEconomy.clusterScopeNote: KDEM tracks Hubballi-Dharwad-Belagavi (HDB) as one cluster of five North Karnataka districts - Belagavi, Dharwad (which includes the Hubballi and Dharwad cities), Bagalkot, Gadag and Haveri. Figures on this tab are for the HDB cluster unless marked otherwise. Targets are from the KDEM HDB Cluster Vision Document 2025, whose horizon year is 2031-32; Karnataka comparison figures are from the KDEM Strategic Dashboard and the Karnataka Economic Survey.

mysuru.heading: HDB's Path: Rs 1,750 Cr to Rs 7,425 Cr by 2031-32
mysuru.sub: The document's baseline is Rs 1,750 Cr (2025-26); 2021-22 to 2024-25 are an estimated back-cast (solid), and the path to 2031-32 (dashed) runs through the document's 2027 waypoint of Rs 3,650 Cr.
mysuru.source: Today (Rs 1,750 Cr, 2025-26) and the path: KDEM HDB Cluster Vision Document 2025 (page 25). History 2021-22 to 2024-25: estimated, GDDP-indexed (Karnataka Economic Survey).
mysuru.methodology: Methodology: today (~Rs 1,750 Cr, 2025-26) is the vision document's baseline. The 2021-22 to 2024-25 history scales that anchor by the HDB cluster's official GDDP series (Rs 1.89 lakh crore in 2020-21 to Rs 2.79 lakh crore in 2023-24, extended two years at ~10% to 2025-26), i.e. the digital economy is assumed to have tracked the district economy - an estimate, for shape only. The dashed path forward runs through the document's own 2027 waypoint (Rs 3,650 Cr) to Rs 7,425 Cr by 2031-32. At Rs 83/USD this is roughly $0.14B to $0.90B.

waterfall.heading: How the Streams Add Up to Rs 7,425 Cr
waterfall.sub: The document gives IT and GCCs as one Rs 5,625 Cr block; here it is split into exports and domestic using Karnataka's 20.5% domestic-to-exports ratio (KDEM Strategic Dashboard), the way the Mysuru tab does. Worth flagging critically: this IT-heavy split arguably understates ESDM, because HDB's biggest confirmed investments are all electronics manufacturing (Aequs Rs 3,540 Cr, EMC 2.0, Nidec Rs 600 Cr) and its engineering talent skews electronics and mechanical (see the stream heat map above). A projection truer to HDB's industrial base would likely weight ESDM higher.

The 2021-22 to 2024-25 history (solid) is an estimate - the Rs 1,250 Cr today scaled backwards by the HDB cluster's official GDDP series (Economic Survey), the same basis as the revenue trajectory above. Publicly, HDB set up or expanded 56 companies over three years (38 new + 18 expanded, KDEM Strategic Dashboard, Mar 2026; 23 new in FY24-25 alone), with early movers Zerodha, Aissel, iMerit and IonIdea cited as creating over 4,000 jobs.

pillarGraphs.methodology: Methodology: today's figure is the live DPIIT-recognised startup count across the five HDB districts on the Startup India portal (accessed 11 Aug 2026): Dharwad 366, Belagavi 332, Bagalkot 63, Gadag 46, Haveri 43 = 850 (a live district filter, so cite with the access date). This already exceeds the KDEM vision document's own 2025 planning figure of 500. The 2021-22 to 2024-25 history (solid) is back-cast at about 20% a year, the recent DPIIT recognition pace - an estimate; only the current 850 is a hard count. The path to the 2,500 vision is a constant-growth line through 2031-32 (about 17% a year), for shape only. Cluster-wide, KDEM reports 400+ operational startups, 80+ funded, 90+ IP filings and 4,500+ jobs over three years (Techceleration 2025), supported by the Deshpande Foundation, KLE-CTIE, K-Tech and IIT/IIIT Dharwad. Startup revenue is a small, modelled stream (the doc's Rs 150 Cr today is 5,000 jobs x Rs 3 lakh/employee off a 500-startup base, so it lags the live count of 850; Rs 750 Cr by 2031-32), so this engine is tracked on counts.

projections.heading: Rs 1,750 Cr Today, Rs 7,425 Cr by 2031-32: What Each Stream Must Do
projections.sub: The 'today' figures are not measured revenue - the KDEM vision document (page 25) models each as employment x average revenue per employee, taking the lower bound of each range. They are only as solid as those two assumptions, and no independent HDB IT-export or ESDM-output figure exists to check them against.

rows.driver: Needs ~25 more mid-size IT firms and 10+ GCCs: spoke-shore units of Bengaluru majors (Infosys, Accenture, HCL, TCS are the named targets) at Aryabhatta Tech Park (Hubballi) and Desur IT Park (Belagavi), scaling on the Hitachi GDC (200 engineers by 2027) and the 4,000+ jobs already at Zerodha, iMerit, IonIdea and Aissel

Rests on plants already committed: the Aequs Rs 3,540 Cr electronics cluster (~20,000 jobs), EMC 2.0 at Kotur-Belur (9 firms, Rs 340 Cr), the Nidec Rs 600 Cr motor plant, and Sankalp / HCLTech's Hubballi chip-design centre coming on stream

Funded by the Rs 1,000 Cr LEAP programme and Rs 25 Cr Cluster Seed Fund, incubated at 11 new TBIs (KLE Tech, VTU/VRIF, Gogte), the Deshpande Foundation sandbox and KLE-CTIE - about 275 net-new DPIIT startups a year from 850 today

totalRow.driver: The three revenue streams KDEM models for the HDB cluster (Vision Document 2025, page 25); a modelled lower estimate, not measured revenue

projections.note: How the today figures are built (KDEM's model, lower bound of each range): IT and GCCs Rs 1,250 Cr = 25,000 jobs x Rs 5 lakh/employee; ESDM Rs 350 Cr = 5,000 jobs x Rs 7 lakh/employee; startups Rs 150 Cr = 5,000 jobs x Rs 3 lakh/employee. These are modelled estimates, not measured revenue - the Rs 5 lakh/employee IT figure is conservative and the headcounts are the document's own. Note those 2025 headcounts (IT 25,000 + ESDM 5,000 + startups 5,000) sum to about 35,000, more than the document's own ~30,000 total-employment figure used in the gauge - an inconsistency in the source, so read the per-stream headcounts as revenue-model inputs, not a workforce census. Implied CAGR is simple arithmetic to the 2031-32 target over seven years. Only these three streams count: unlike the Mysuru tab (a bottom-up $10B build on KDEM's 5-stream dashboard), the HDB vision document's Rs 7,425 Cr has no digitizing-sectors or biotech line, and KDEM publishes digitizing only Beyond-Bengaluru-wide, so neither is shown here. The startup base is shown as the live DPIIT count (850); the Rs 150 Cr revenue is the document's separate 500-startup modelled basis.
projections.source: KDEM HDB Cluster Vision Document 2025 (page 25), published on the KDEM resource page; KDEM's own planning figures, not independently verified

digitalEconomy.storiesSub: HDB-cluster companies with real, verified numbers

stories.title: Vayavya Labs - Belagavi
stories.subtitle: Automotive silicon software from North Karnataka, drawing a Rs 245 Cr deal
stories.body: Founded in Belagavi in 2006, Vayavya Labs builds software for the hardware-software interface in vehicles - virtual ECUs and digital twins, verification and validation for ADAS and autonomous driving, and software-defined-vehicle architectures. It was named in Forbes India's Top 200 Global Business Potential list, with turnover of about Rs 66 Cr in FY25 rising to Rs 83 Cr in FY26. In April 2026, listed chip firm MosChip agreed to acquire a 73% stake for Rs 245.49 Cr (Rs 148.52 Cr cash plus equity). As of August 2026 the deal is not yet closed - it is stalled under a Supreme Court status-quo order and the shareholder meeting was postponed.
stories.significance: A Belagavi-headquartered chip-software company built globally competitive automotive silicon IP and drew a Rs 245 Cr acquisition offer (announced April 2026, not yet closed)
stories.source: MosChip deal + FY26 turnover: MosChip disclosure / YourStory / ScanX (Apr-May 2026); deal pending under a Supreme Court status-quo order. FY25 revenue: Tracxn.

series.label: Turnover (Rs Cr)

KDEM tracks the Hubballi centre growing from about 250 to around 600 people, serving autonomous-vehicle, agri and medical AI clients.

talentSection.heading: The Talent Base: 35,000+ Students a Year

talentSection.methodology: Methodology: the KDEM year-wise plan sets total cluster employment at about 30,000 (2025-26), 45,000 (2026-27), 60,000 (2028-29) and 1,00,000 (2029-30), rising to 1,50,000 by 2031-32. The 2021-22 to 2024-25 history (solid) is back-cast from the ~30,000 baseline at about 12% a year - an estimate, for shape only. The pipeline is fed by 200+ colleges producing 35,000+ graduates a year, including IIT Dharwad, IIIT Dharwad and KLE Technological University, with skilling through the Deshpande Foundation, FUEL, NTTF, Nipuna and NASSCOM FutureSkills.

talentHeatmap.heading: Where the Engineers Are: Stream Concentration by District
talentHeatmap.sub: Share of engineering seats by branch, from the Karnataka KEA UGCET-2026 final seat matrix. The HDB districts are far less CS-dominated than Bengaluru and far more concentrated in electronics and mechanical - the exact talent base for ESDM, auto-electronics and EVs.
talentHeatmap.note: Cells are shaded by concentration versus the Karnataka average (darker = a bigger share of that district's seats than the state as a whole). This is why the HDB districts glow in electronics and mechanical while Bengaluru glows in CS. Electronics groups ECE and Electrical/EEE. Built by parsing the KEA UGCET-2026 final engineering seat matrix (163 colleges, ~95,000 seats); 73% of colleges reconcile exactly against their printed totals and branch shares are stable. The HDB cluster's electronics + mechanical share is 38%, against 28% in Bengaluru and 32% statewide. The 21 colleges shown for HDB are the engineering colleges in the KCET counselling matrix (a subset of the cluster's ~43 engineering and 200+ total colleges); autonomous, deemed and private-university colleges outside that matrix are not counted here.
talentHeatmap.source: Karnataka Examinations Authority (KEA), UGCET-2026 final engineering seat matrix (30-06-2026)

digitalEconomy.sourceNote: Sourcing note: the Rs 1,750 / 3,650 / 7,425 Cr revenue path, the stream splits and the per-stream and 1,00,000-1,50,000 jobs figures are the KDEM HDB Cluster Vision Document's own projection - published by KDEM on its resource page (karnatakadigital.in/resource/) but not independently verified by any third party, and labelled as such on each card. What IS publicly reported (Techceleration 2025) is a Rs 1,000+ Cr investment framework and a 2,500-startup roadmap. 2031-32 is the document's near-term projection year; the broader HDB roadmap extends to 2047 (India@100), and 2031-32 is separately Karnataka's statewide $329B digital-economy target year. Cluster GDP is from the Karnataka Economic Survey; the engineering-stream heat map is from the KEA seat matrix; company, policy and ecosystem figures are sourced on each card, with the method, source date or live-access date stated where a figure is an estimate, a live count or a draft projection.
